facts.fact: La Nation reports a public primary school head in Cotonou entering her pupils on Educmaster on 18 December 2024, and says every public and private collège and lycée must enter its school-life data on the platform.

At primary level the head of EPP Gbégamey group B, Cotonou, says the school's role is to enrol and record every learner and the supervising staff in the platform's database so as to follow their path; on 18 December 2024 she was a quarter of the way through the first-year (CI) intake, slowed by pupils without birth certificates, with the other classes already entered.

At secondary level the ministry's information systems director says collèges and lycées enter enrolments, transfers, absences, timetables and pupil numbers per class, and load each pupil's end-of-semester averages, with individual marks to follow in a new version; no transfer is accepted unless made through the platform.

La Nation says Educmaster was launched in 2018 and set up by the Ministère des Enseignements secondaire, technique et de la Formation professionnelle, whose information systems directorate speaks for it and announces a new version.

The article gives no number or share of primary schools entering data: it shows one public primary school in Cotonou registering its learners, and for secondary says all public and private collèges and lycées are required to use the platform, which is an obligation and not a count of schools entering.
